generatedProse.concept-context: In practice, revising on purpose runs across a whole module, not just the week before the exam. You plan your time around your gaps, revise each topic actively, and pick a technique that fits it, then re-test and adjust. Each round feeds the next, so the practice improves as you go.
generatedProse.worked-example: Two students revise the same module. One makes a tidy timetable and re-reads every topic for an equal block of time. The other tests herself first, gives her weak topics the most time, revises them actively, and picks a technique to fit each one. By the exam, the second student knows her weak topics well, because she ran the three ideas as one practice.
generatedProse.summary: Revising on purpose is most useful when the three ideas work as one practice. You plan around your time and gaps, revise actively, and choose techniques that fit the material, then repeat and adjust across the module. It is the practice, not any single session, that gets you ready for the exam.

check.body: A student lists her topics, tests herself to find the weak ones, gives them the most time, and revises each with a technique chosen to fit it. What does this show?

items.text: Their next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following essay improved.
Nothing; feedback comes at the end, so it cannot affect anything that follows.

feedback.correct: That's right. Using feedback to plan the next piece of work feeds it straight back into your learning, closing the loop and starting the next round stronger. That is the cycle working as it should.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Think about what the student did with the feedback, and what improved as a result.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Acting on feedback feeds your next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following essay was stronger. The mark on the first essay cannot change, but the feedback still shapes what comes next.

_items.text: One revision practice at work: a strategy built on time and gaps, filled with active revision and techniques that fit the material.
_items.feedback: Yes. All three ideas are running together as one practice.

_items.text: That she is spending too long on revision and should cut it down.
_items.feedback: The point is not how long she spends. It is that the three ideas work together.

_items.text: That the technique she picks is the only thing that matters.
_items.feedback: The technique only helps because the strategy pointed it at a weak topic first.

_items.text: That she has skipped planning and gone straight to revising.
_items.feedback: She planned first: she found her gaps and budgeted her time before revising.

_prompts.concept-context: What does this look like in practice within the given context? Write a short follow-on from the generic definition above, in the learner's own subject or discipline. Keep it to two or three sentences, mid-register, following straight on from the generic definition.
_prompts.worked-example: Give a subject-specific worked example of this lesson's concept: a weaker or less-developed version first, then a stronger version reached by better practice, using the context cast (character tokens) consistently. Keep the weaker-then-stronger shape and the two-part contrast; name the cast directly in the prose (the pack supplies the whole body). The merge renders it as a block quote, so write it as continuous prose, not as a quoted comment plus commentary.
_prompts.summary: Recap what the learner can now do, in terms of their own subject or context. One short paragraph. Do not restate the learning outcomes verbatim.
_prompts.check: Write the subject's own version of this lesson's check question(s), testing the same outcome in the learner's own discipline. Keep the same number of items and the same correctness pattern as the generic version; reword the stem and items for the subject.
